cost: O(argument bytes + VFS operation work); delete adds O(number of paths) sequential stat/remove calls; listing retains O(entries + name bytes). No transaction, allocation or traversal cap is added here.
description: Filesystem builtins dispatch through Interp.fs: file/dir predicates, directory creation/removal, sequential deletion, move/copy and directory listing.
forward: F(op,args,n,fs) validates path strings then performs the selected trait operation. mkdir/rmdir/move/copy return no result on successful n=0, true status for n>0; trait errors throw for n=0 and become false/message for n>0. delete processes paths left-to-right; readdir returns dot entries plus provider order.
inverse: For valid path strings, an FsError from rmdir with n>0 excludes a thrown MError; the same FsError with n=0 excludes false-return success. delete(directory) excludes remove_file(directory), but does not exclude earlier successful deletions.

Successful status has all compatible VFS antecedents permitting the requested operation, including already-existing mkdir directories. exist_path=0 includes every stat error, not just absence; status/messages cannot reconstruct original filesystem contents.
limitations: Partial source-bound model, not semantic proof
Finite synthetic fixtures only; frozen suites/external measurement unexecuted
state: exist_path uses 7 for directories, 2 for any other stat success, 0 for error. readdir prepends . and .. and delegates remaining ordering to provider. Recursive rmdir is enabled only by second string equal to s.
